decisions.summary: joined_link: the straight snap where walkable, else the clear run the far-gap branch lays, else the run is refused; a carried end spliced on by carried_onto, which also checks the leg from the run's next vertex into a clear-run link that does not start at the end
decisions.why: Row 486's ranked fix word for word, and it meets wave 43 round 2's condition that the routed link is tried before the refusal. carried_onto (the round 1 aside) closes the one way the splice could put ink on ground that was never checked: a clear run starts past the foul it skirted. It is tested (test_carried_onto_splices_the_link_and_checks_the_leg_into_it). Refusal now happens only where no walkable link exists, which is 0081's own 'or the lane not drawn'.

decisions.summary: A run kept whole (both halves 40 ft or more) has three outcomes: run[k] snapped onto its foot where both new legs are walkable; else joined_link's link drawn as its own join lane (_draw_web(..., joins=True)) beside the whole run; else not drawn
decisions.why: Round 1 ruled this NOT LEGITIMATE on two carve-outs, and both are gone from serve.py. (a) The snap no longer depends on joined_link(run[k], q): it is decided by the two new legs alone, so a run is no longer refused for an obstacle on a link it never draws. (b) Where a leg is blocked, the link joined_link finds is drawn as its own lane, the way the far-gap branch draws one. The run is refused only where there is no link, or where the link cannot be drawn. The claim at serve.py now reads 'not drawn where no link is walkable'. test_a_run_kept_whole_takes_a_link_where_it_arrives covers the snap, the drawn link (red on the old code, which returned False) and the refusal. A test of (a) on its own (p->q blocked, both legs clear) is not among them; the code reading is unambiguous, so that is an aside.
